title: Waiting by the Stump for a Hare
text:
In the state of Song there was a farmer who had a tree stump standing in the middle of his field. One day, while he was working, a hare came racing across the field, ran headlong into the stump, broke its neck and died.

The farmer picked it up and took it home. It was a free meal, gained without any effort at all. It seemed to him a much better way to get food than plowing.

So he put down his plow and stopped working the field. Every day he sat beside the stump and waited for another hare to come running into it. Days passed, then weeks. No hare came. His field went to weeds, and he became the laughingstock of the whole state of Song.

The philosopher Han Fei, who told this story in the third century BC, used it against the rulers of his day who wanted to govern by copying the methods of the ancient sage kings. Times had changed, he argued. Hoping that the old ways would work again because they once worked was exactly like waiting by the stump for another hare.
lesson: Do not build a strategy on a single lucky outcome. What worked once by chance, or in a different age, needs to be tested again before you bet on it.
